$comment: Source registry. Every event and every map overlay must cite sources by `id`. `verification` records what has actually been checked in this repository. Do NOT add page numbers to events unless a team member has seen the page. Tiers: primary = chronicle/treaty/eyewitness; scholarly = peer-reviewed or standard academic history; official = government/UNESCO/museum; reference = encyclopaedia; finding-aid = may be used to locate sources but never as sole support for a claim.

sources.title: A History of Assam
otherEditions: 3rd edition 1963, revised by B. K. Barua and H. V. S. Murthy
sources.notes: Foundational narrative and regnal chronology derived largely from Buranjis. Colonial-era interpretive framing; cross-check against Barpujari (ed.) and later scholarship. Two archive.org scans exist; which corresponds to the 1906 Thacker, Spink printing is not yet confirmed. Edition matters for page numbers: cite edition with every page.
sources.access: public-domain scan (archive.org) - blocked from the Phase 1 build environment

sources.title: Ahom-Buranji: From the Earliest Time to the End of Ahom Rule
sources.publisher: Assam Government / printed at the Baptist Mission Press
sources.notes: Tai-Ahom text with English translation. Primary chronicle in translation; chronicle dates are converted from Tai cyclical reckoning and should be treated as chronicle-derived. Catalogues differ on pagination (388 vs 395 pp.).

sources.title: The Comprehensive History of Assam
volumesRelevant: Vol. 2: Medieval period, political - from the thirteenth century A.D. to the Treaty of Yandabo, 1826
Vol. 3: Medieval period - administrative, economic, social and cultural
sources.notes: Series began 1990; individual volume years NOT yet verified - record the volume year from the physical copy. Multi-author chapters: cite chapter author + volume + page. Later 5-volume edition (Assam Prakashan Parishad, 2022 per bookseller listing) has different pagination.

sources.title: A Comprehensive History of Assam
sources.notes: Reprinted 1997 and later; ISBN varies by printing (9788121500159 on a 2023 reprint). Cite printing used.

sources.title: Medieval and Early Colonial Assam: Society, Polity, Economy
sources.publisher: K. P. Bagchi & Co. for the Centre for Studies in Social Sciences, Calcutta
sources.physical: xviii, 309 p. (HathiTrust); NEHU record gives xvii, 307 p.
sources.notes: Collected essays on the Ahom state, paik system, economy, and early colonial transition. Key for 'state formation' and 'institutional breakdown' framing; NOT a narrative chronology.

sources.title: The Tai and the Tai Kingdoms, with a Fuller Treatment of the Tai-Ahom Kingdom in the Brahmaputra Valley
sources.notes: Based on the author's 1961 Gauhati University thesis. Principal English-language scholarly treatment of the wider Tai world (Mong Mao etc.) for Episode 1 and the migration.

sources.title: Lachit Barphukan and His Times: A History of the Assam-Mogul Conflicts of the Period 1667 to 1671 A.D.
sources.publisher: Government of Assam, Department of Historical and Antiquarian Studies
sources.notes: Primary scholarly study of the 1667-1671 campaigns, built from Buranjis. Historiographical note: later scholars observe it helped give the Lachit narrative academic respectability; treat heroic details as tradition unless independently attested.

sources.title: Anglo-Assamese Relations, 1771-1826
sources.publisher: Department of Historical and Antiquarian Studies in Assam
sources.notes: Based on English and Assamese archival sources; key for the Welsh expedition (1792-94), Burmese invasions and 1824-26.

sources.title: Fragmented Memories: Struggling to be Tai-Ahom in India
sources.notes: Use for historiography and modern memory of Ahom identity - important caveat material for narration (how the Ahom past is remembered and politically used today). Not a source for medieval event dates.

sources.title: Moidams - the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty (inscription, 46th session, New Delhi, July 2024)
sources.notes: Inscription confirmed via multiple news reports (e.g. AP via ABC News, 26 July 2024). TODO: replace list URL with the exact WHC property page and nomination dossier URL once fetched; the WHC host was not checked in Phase 1.

authors: East India Company and Kingdom of Ava
sources.title: Treaty of Peace concluded at Yandabo, 24 February 1826
sources.notes: Article 2 (as quoted in the Cambridge reproduction): the King of Ava 'renounces all claims upon, and will abstain from all future interference with, the principality of Assam and its dependencies, and also with the contiguous petty states of Cachar and Jyntea'. Narration must say Burma RENOUNCED claims; it is debated whether this is a formal cession of Assam to the Company. sources.access: Cambridge (paywalled); Aitchison volumes in public domain

authors: Ministry of Culture, Government of India - Indian Culture portal
sources.title: Battle of Saraighat
sources.notes: Government heritage story. Gives 1671, Raja Ram Singh vs Lachit Borphukan. Repeats the poppy-seed anecdote - that anecdote must be labelled TRADITIONAL in our narration.

authors: Kamrup (Metro/Rural) District Administration, Government of Assam
sources.title: The Battle of Alaboi and the Battle of Saraighat
sources.notes: District government page. Reportedly dates Saraighat to 1672, disagreeing with the 1671 consensus - recorded here as evidence of a dating discrepancy, not as authority.

sources.title: Fathiyya-i-Ibriyya (Persian account of Mir Jumla's Assam campaign, 1661-63)
sources.notes: Eyewitness Mughal-side account. English translation/edition NOT yet located or verified. Do not cite until an edition (translator, journal/publisher, year, page) is confirmed.

sources.title: Report on Assam (1794)
sources.notes: Eyewitness East India Company report from the 1792-94 expedition. Published edition NOT yet verified (believed reproduced in later compilations). Access via bhuyan1949 until located.

authors: Philippe Vandermaelen (attribution inferred from sheet format)
sources.title: Asie No. 84 - Assam et Boutan (Atlas universel)
sources.notes: Reference image supplied by the user. Sheet header 'ASIE / ASSAM ET BOUTAN / No. 84' matches the format of Vandermaelen's Atlas universel (Brussels, 1825-27); attribution and year must be confirmed from a catalogue record. Use ONLY as a georeferencing aid for early-19th-century European geographic knowledge (river names, settlement placement). Its colour bands are a European cartographer's view, not authoritative political boundaries.
